subject: math.NT
name: Euclid’s theorem on primes
statement: There are infinitely many prime numbers.

subject: math.NT
name: Fundamental theorem of arithmetic
statement: Every integer greater than 1 has a prime factorization that is unique up to the order of the prime factors.

subject: math.NT
name: Bézout’s identity
statement: For integers a and b not both zero, there exist integers x and y such that ax+by=gcd(a,b). Every integer linear combination of a and b is divisible by gcd(a,b).

subject: math.NT
name: Chinese remainder theorem
statement: For pairwise relatively prime positive integers m₁,…,mᵣ and any integers a₁,…,aᵣ, there exists an integer x satisfying x ≡ aᵢ modulo mᵢ for every i. The solution is unique modulo m₁⋯mᵣ.

subject: math.NT
name: Fermat’s little theorem
statement: If p is prime and a is an integer not divisible by p, then a^(p−1) ≡ 1 modulo p. For every integer a, aᵖ ≡ a modulo p.

subject: math.NT
name: Euler’s theorem
statement: If n is a positive integer and gcd(a,n)=1, then a^φ(n) ≡ 1 modulo n, where φ(n) is Euler’s totient function.

subject: math.NT
name: Wilson’s theorem
statement: An integer p>1 is prime if and only if (p−1)! ≡ −1 modulo p.

subject: math.NT
name: Quadratic reciprocity
statement: For distinct odd primes p and q, the Legendre symbols satisfy (p/q)(q/p)=(−1)^((p−1)(q−1)/4). The Legendre symbol (a/p) is 1 if a is a nonzero square modulo p, −1 if it is a nonsquare, and 0 if p divides a.

subject: math.NT
name: Dirichlet’s theorem on arithmetic progressions
statement: If a and d are relatively prime positive integers, then the arithmetic progression a,a+d,a+2d,… contains infinitely many primes.

subject: math.NT
name: Prime number theorem
statement: Let π(x) denote the number of primes at most x. Then π(x)/(x/log x) tends to 1 as x tends to infinity, where log denotes the natural logarithm.

subject: math.NT
name: Bertrand’s postulate
statement: For every integer n>1, there exists a prime p with n<p<2n.

subject: math.NT
name: Lagrange’s four-square theorem
statement: Every nonnegative integer can be written as a sum of four integer squares.

subject: math.NT
name: Sum of two squares theorem
statement: A positive integer n is a sum of two integer squares if and only if every prime congruent to 3 modulo 4 occurs to an even exponent in the prime factorization of n.

subject: math.NT
name: Pell equation theorem
statement: For every positive integer D that is not a perfect square, x²−Dy²=1 has a solution in positive integers. If (x₁,y₁) is the solution with smallest x₁>1, all positive solutions are given by xₖ+yₖ√D=(x₁+y₁√D)ᵏ for integers k≥1.

subject: math.NT
name: Minkowski’s convex body theorem
statement: If Λ is a full-rank lattice in ℝⁿ and C is a convex set symmetric about the origin whose n-dimensional volume exceeds 2ⁿ times the volume of a fundamental cell of Λ, then C contains a nonzero lattice point.

subject: math.NT
name: Liouville’s approximation theorem
statement: If α is a real algebraic number of degree d≥2 over the rationals, there is a constant C>0 such that |α−p/q| ≥ C/qᵈ for all integers p and positive integers q.

subject: math.NT
name: Roth’s theorem
statement: If α is a real algebraic irrational number, then for every ε>0 there are only finitely many relatively prime integers p,q with q>0 satisfying |α−p/q|<1/q^(2+ε).

subject: math.NT
name: Hasse’s theorem on elliptic curves
statement: If E is an elliptic curve over a finite field with q elements, then |#E(𝔽_q)−(q+1)| ≤ 2√q, where the count includes the point at infinity.

subject: math.NT
name: Fermat’s last theorem
statement: For every integer n>2, there are no positive integers a,b,c satisfying aⁿ+bⁿ=cⁿ.

subject: math.NT
name: Hensel’s lemma for simple roots
statement: Let p be prime and f a polynomial with coefficients in the p-adic integers ℤ_p. If a∈ℤ_p satisfies f(a) ≡ 0 modulo p and f′(a) is not divisible by p, then there is a unique b∈ℤ_p with b ≡ a modulo p and f(b)=0.
